title: Determination of QTc-Time in newborns, premature infants, infants and school children using different correction formulas with a view to early detection of Long-QT-Syndrom
summary:
We are studying the so-called QT interval in ECGs. An ECG records the electrical conduction in the heart muscle, where the individual waves and curves correspond to the different phases of cardiac activity (excitation and relaxation) of the ventricles. These time intervals are labeled alphabetically. The so-called QT interval provides information about the electrical recovery phase of the heart, i.e., the relaxation phase of the heart.
This QT interval depends on the heart rate. Therefore, in order to assess it for potential diseases, formulas are needed to correct it for heart rate. If it is prolonged, it is associated with an increased risk of cardiac arrhythmias and should therefore be detected as early as possible.
Currently, the Bazett formula is commonly used, but it has only been validated in adults. Adults have a lower heart rate than newborns and infants. This suggests that there may be a more suitable formula for pediatric patients. In order to compare different formulas effectively, we aim to examine as large a number as possible of healthy newborns and premature infants using ECG.
The goal of our work is to identify the most appropriate correction formula for pediatric patients in order to detect cardiac conduction disorders or dangerous arrhythmias, such as long QT syndrome (LQTS), early and accurately.

interventions.name: Prospective intervention study: single 12-channel ECG (50/mm/sec) in approximately 100 newborns (0-30 days) and approximately 100 preterm infants (<37 weeks gestation), comparison of different correction formulas for calculating the QTc-time

Additionally, retrospective data analysis of approximately 1,000 ECGs from infants (per month age approximately 100 ECGs per 10 heart rate beats of approximately 120-220bpm) for comparison of different correction formulas for calculating the QTc-time.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Prospectively: Premature/ newborns without prenatal or perinatal diagnosed heart disease may participate after informed consent and written consent from the parents.
Retrospectively: None
Exclusion criteria:
Prospectively: children with prenatally diagnosed heart defects or without parental consent will be excluded from the study.
Retrospectively: None.
